messages:
Maria: quick check — for private deployments, are we leaning toward ephemeral peering per-tenant or a regional relay proxy for tenant egress? thinking about cost + churn tradeoffs
Jon: leaning relay. per-tenant peering looks clean for isolation but costs explode (peer setup, route limits). relay gives amortized egress ip and simpler NAT table usage
Kevin: +1 on cost concern. also route table scale: AWS account route limit + RDS of routes per TGW. If we do per-tenant peering we need route aggregation or big infra work
Ryan: curious about lifecycle model if we pick ephemeral peering: how long live, reconnect strategy, health checks, and what happens during CP outage? ephemeral peering can be torn down on idle but must reattach fast for bursty tenants
Tanya: operationally a relay lets us do per-tenant ACLs at app layer and keeps control plane smaller. downside: single proxy failure blast radius unless we shard by tenant affinity and use failover relays
Maria: what about a hybrid? ephemeral peering for high-compliance tenants, regional relay for others. need heuristics to classify tenants automatically
Jon: hybrid sounds pragmatic. heuristics could be tier + SLA flag. But we also need eviction policy for ephemeral peers to reclaim IP space and routes
Kevin: eviction/idle policy: keep peer active while 95th percentile of requests in last 24h > threshold OR active connections > N. fallback to relay with sticky routing when peer is offlined
Ryan: technical notes: peering lifecycle states: PROVISIONING -> ACTIVE -> IDLE -> DRAINING -> TEARDOWN. Must preserve VIP mapping during DRAINING to avoid in-flight token invalidation. Also add pre-warm step for bursty tenants
Tanya: monitoring checklist: peer attach latency histogram, route program failures, NAT allocation rate, flow logs showing egress ip churn. Add alert on peer reattach > X/sec
sre-bot: metric report stub: peer_attach_50p=1.3s peer_attach_95p=4.8s nat_alloc_rate=12/min last_24h (synthetic)
Maria: rollout plan draft: 1) implement relay as baseline (no infra changes) 2) gated feature: ephemeral peering for selected beta tenants 3) automate heuristics + dashboard 4) opt-in for compliance customers
Jon: questions for cost modeling: how to charge tenants? ledger per egress ip-hour? or absorb and meter by tokens/throughput? both have ops implications
Kevin: suggest we model two axes: infra cost of peer (route entries, ENIs, NAT) + ops cost (incidents per attach). run simulation on last 90d traffic with current tenant distribution
Ryan: snippet for attach script idea — will post prototype later, but core is: create route, attach peer, warm TCP/HTTP probes, then flip affinity. pseudo:
```
# attach flow
create_vpc_peer(tid)
program_routes(tid)
warm_probes(tid, 10)
set_affinity(tid, peer_id)
```
Tanya: rollback playbook: if attach fails repeatedly -> mark tenant to use relay and auto-create incident with engineer on-call. Also allow manual override from console
Maria: OK next actions: Ryan to prototype attach state machine, Kevin to run cost sim, Tanya to define monitoring/alerts, Jon to run billing model. I'll coordinate with ProdEng for beta tenants :thumbsup:
Jon: noted. timeline request: can we aim prototype in 2 weeks?
Ryan: yes, I'll have a basic state machine + logs in 2w
Kevin: cost sim will need infra logs, I'll take 7 days after access
Tanya: I'll draft alert rules today and share on #eng-sre
Maria: thanks all — will follow up with a short RFC and link to this thread
